name: Shemaiah
overview: Shemaiah was a male member of the tribe of Simeon, noted in Scripture primarily as the father of Shimri. His identity is grounded in his Simeonite heritage, reflecting his place within the genealogical records of Israel. Beyond this, the biblical text does not provide additional personal details or notable events associated with him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemaiah means 'YHWH hears,' indicating a theophoric element that acknowledges God's attentive presence. This proper name, recorded in 1 Chronicles 4:37, does not appear to have been given directly by God but carries a meaningful declaration of divine attentiveness.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture records Shemaiah as the father of Shimri, establishing a direct familial link within the Simeonite lineage. No other family relationships are documented beyond this connection in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Shemaiah's significance in the biblical narrative lies in his role as an ancestor within the tribe of Simeon, contributing to the preservation of Israel's genealogical history. His mention underscores the faithfulness of God in maintaining His people through successive generations, as reflected in the detailed family records of 1 Chronicles. Though not prominent in major events, his inclusion affirms the importance of lineage and heritage in God's redemptive plan.
